requirement: One natural person SHALL map to one durable canonical person identity unless the identity remains explicitly unresolved or disputed.
An account SHALL belong to one controlling identity and SHALL NOT substitute for legal, personal, organizational, guardian, ownership, or relationship truth.
External identity providers MAY authenticate but SHALL NOT determine EquineSync roles, relationships, permissions, representation, or authority.

Every consequential action SHALL preserve the authenticated principal, acting principal, represented principal where applicable, approving actor, executing actor, tenant context, session, and relevant evidence.
A person MAY participate in multiple tenants through one durable identity, but each tenant SHALL independently govern membership, roles, visibility, billing, communications, and audit.
Global identity resolution SHALL NOT expose tenant-specific data or confirm another tenant relationship to an unauthorized actor.
Invitation issuance SHALL create no operational authority until the invitation is validly accepted, required checks are completed, and the membership or relationship is activated.
Invitation tokens SHALL be single-use, revocable, purpose-bound, stored only in protected form, and expire under an approved security policy.
Onboarding SHALL progressively collect only information necessary for the current step and SHALL NOT require users to understand the entire ecosystem before receiving value.
The platform SHALL distinguish person identity, authentication method, role, organization, horse relationship, billing responsibility, and permission authority throughout enrollment.
Role or membership assignment SHALL NOT by itself establish legal authority, ownership, guardianship, professional authority, or unrestricted access.
Horse profile creation, payment activity, barn membership, emergency-contact status, or record possession SHALL NOT establish horse ownership, custody, care authority, or record access.
Payment details or payment performance SHALL NOT establish guardian status, legal responsibility, signing capacity, ownership, or permission authority.
A minor or protected participant SHALL retain a distinct identity separate from every guardian, payer, coach, trainer, and household account.
Guardians and minors SHALL use separate accounts and credentials; shared credentials, invisible guardian takeover, and trainer use of a guardian account SHALL be prohibited.
Guardian authority SHALL be evidenced, scoped, effective-dated, revocable, and reassessed upon material lifecycle changes.
A minor account SHALL receive only age-appropriate, purpose-limited capabilities and SHALL NOT inherit unrestricted billing, medical, legal, safeguarding, ownership, or administrative access.
Ordinary one-to-one electronic communication between a minor and an adult third party SHALL remain unavailable through enrollment or account configuration.
High-risk identity actions SHALL require stronger assurance, explicit authority, and additional audit evidence.
Sessions SHALL preserve account, authenticated identity, assurance level, tenant context, device, representation, risk, issue time, expiry, and revocation state.
Account restriction, suspension, closure, and compromise states SHALL not erase identity, authorship, historical relationships, accrued obligations, or evidence.
Account recovery SHALL be risk-proportionate, resistant to enumeration and takeover, fully audited, and incapable of silently restoring revoked relationships or privileged authority.
A disputed identity or authority claim SHALL be visibly classified and SHALL NOT be silently normalized into verified truth.
Organization actions SHALL preserve the named human or machine actor and represented organization.
Shared organization passwords SHALL be prohibited.

Agreement execution during enrollment SHALL preserve signer identity, account, assurance level, represented party, capacity, guardian status, authority evidence, agreement version, method, and execution time.
Enrollment and security communications SHALL identify the governing context, sender or automated source, recipient, delivery state, and response or escalation path.

Identity and enrollment data SHALL be minimized, purpose-limited, classified, and separated into required, optional, verification, organization-visible, support-visible, and highly restricted categories.
Identity verification SHALL be represented as scoped evidence and confidence, and SHALL NOT be treated as universal authorization.
Onboarding SHALL be complete only when the enrolled tenant or participant can perform the approved primary end-to-end workflow, not merely display a completed profile.

Authentication-method changes, account recovery, role elevation, identity merge, tenant-owner activation, and support-access activation SHALL require online confirmation and SHALL NOT be completed solely offline.
The interface SHALL expose clear loading, invitation-expired, duplicate-detected, verification-pending, access-denied, recovery-pending, offline, sync-pending, and support-escalation states.

Enrollment interfaces SHALL be accessible, mobile-responsive, readable in field conditions, and capable of preserving progress through interruption without silently accepting incomplete legal or authority steps.
All material identity lifecycle events SHALL generate structured, attributable audit events with prior state, new state, reason, authority source, and relevant evidence references.

The platform SHALL monitor enrollment failures, invitation failures, recovery abuse, unusual privilege changes, session revocations, and cross-tenant access denials without exposing sensitive data in logs.
Every first-user enrollment requirement SHALL map to an acceptance criterion, positive test, negative or abuse test where applicable, and preserved evidence.
A relationship SHALL NOT be inferred solely from a role label, account, email, payment, invoice, possession, profile creation, task assignment, or UI placement.
The system SHALL distinguish asserted, provisional, verified, active, suspended, disputed, ended, superseded, and archived relationship states.
A relationship record SHALL preserve effective time, recorded time, created-by actor, source, confidence or verification, and supersession history.
Relationship state SHALL NOT itself bypass authorization evaluation or create unrestricted access.
The system SHALL distinguish organization, tenant, facility, location, program, and colloquial barn contexts.
One organization MAY operate multiple programs, facilities, or locations without automatically creating separate tenants.
Person-to-organization relationships SHALL identify role context, employment or contractor status, facility scope, horse scope, start/end dates, manager where applicable, and offboarding policy.
Person-to-horse relationships SHALL distinguish ownership, co-ownership, lease, custody, training, riding, care, provider, emergency, and historical relationships.
Creating or importing a horse record SHALL NOT establish ownership, custody, possession, or care authority.
Current possession, boarding location, payment, or record stewardship SHALL NOT independently establish legal ownership.
Care Circle participation SHALL be distinct from ownership, custody, guardianship, medical authority, financial responsibility, and universal record access.
Emergency-contact relationships SHALL grant notification priority only unless a separate authority basis exists.
Guardian relationships SHALL support multiple guardians with independent scopes, restrictions, effective periods, documentary evidence, conflicts, and continuing-guardianship exceptions.
Payment responsibility SHALL NOT establish guardian authority, custody, consent capacity, or general record access.
Protected-participant rules MAY narrow or prohibit a relationship or delegation even when the relationship otherwise exists.
A delegate SHALL NOT receive more authority than the delegator currently holds.
Delegation SHALL be limited by approved action registry, subject, horse, organization, facility, record, purpose, financial limit, effective start, and effective end as applicable.
Delegation SHALL end or be suspended when its source authority ends, is suspended, expires, or becomes disputed unless an approved independent basis exists.
Redelegation SHALL be prohibited by default and permitted only through an explicit governed rule with a bounded limit.
Shared credentials SHALL NOT be used as a substitute for delegation.
Delegation SHALL NOT expose unrelated records or create general horse-record, medical, custody, financial, or administrative authority.

Delegate identity verification and acceptance SHALL be required before activation where the delegation creates duties, access, safety obligations, financial limits, or protected-participant interaction.
Delegation revocation SHALL be effective-dated, attributable, auditable, and propagated to authorization, sessions, offline state, integrations, exports, and dependent delegations as applicable.
Relationship invitations and claims SHALL remain provisional until required identity, agreement, evidence, and authority checks complete.
Multiple concurrent relationships SHALL be preserved when scopes differ or authority is shared.
Conflicting relationship assertions SHALL be visibly classified and routed to controlled review rather than resolved by last-write-wins behavior.
A challenge SHALL NOT automatically establish the challenger's claimed relationship or suspend necessary protective controls.
Temporary protective restrictions SHALL be separable from final relationship adjudication and shall be time-limited, reviewable, attributable, and minimum necessary.
Ending a relationship SHALL prospectively remove its operational effects while preserving historical authorship, evidence, accrued obligations, and prior valid actions.
Reactivation SHALL reevaluate current identity, relationship, agreement, restrictions, and permission state rather than restoring former access automatically.
Relationship changes SHALL generate structured audit events recording prior state, new state, actor, authority source, effective time, reason, and evidence references.
Relationship search and discovery SHALL expose only minimum information needed for the active workflow and SHALL NOT reveal unrelated tenant, guardian, ownership, dispute, or safeguarding data.
High-risk relationship changes SHALL require stronger assurance, explicit authority, and additional review or approval as defined by Identity and Authorization controls.
Relationship creation, acceptance, revocation, dispute, and termination requiring authoritative state SHALL complete online and SHALL NOT rely solely on stale offline state.
The platform SHALL monitor unusual delegation volume, repeated failed relationship claims, conflicting ownership assertions, stale revocation propagation, and privileged relationship changes.
Every first-user relationship requirement SHALL map to acceptance criteria, positive tests, negative or abuse tests where applicable, and preserved evidence.
Legal title, beneficial interest, custody, operational control, care responsibility, financial responsibility, and record stewardship SHALL remain distinguishable.
Verification SHALL be claim-specific, evidence-specific, purpose-specific, and time-bounded; it SHALL NOT create a universal verified status.
Delegation and dependent authority SHALL preserve an explicit source-authority dependency graph and the exact source versions used for activation and action evaluation.
Delegation dependency cycles SHALL be prohibited and detected before activation and during every material dependency change.
A material change to an accepted delegation SHALL create a new immutable grant version or replacement grant rather than silently mutating the accepted scope.
Delegation renewal SHALL revalidate current source authority, restrictions, assurance, and protected-participant constraints and SHALL require fresh acceptance when material duties or risks change.
Relationship visibility SHALL be produced through purpose-specific privacy projections and SHALL not expose the full relationship graph by default.
Consequential actions SHALL record the exact relationship, delegation, source-authority, restriction, and type-registry versions used by Authorization.
Relationship events and audit evidence SHALL be emitted atomically with the authoritative mutation or the mutation SHALL fail closed or enter a controlled quarantine state.
Retroactive correction SHALL preserve the recorded history and SHALL NOT erase actions validly attributable under the prior known state.
Self-verification, self-approval, and self-delegation in high-risk relationship workflows SHALL be prohibited or routed to an expressly governed independent review path.
